definitions: A member of the Germanic peoples (Angles, Saxons, and Jutes) who settled in Britain in the 5th and 6th centuries.
The period of English history when the Anglo-Saxons were dominant, from the 5th century to the Norman Conquest in 1066.
examples: The Anglo-Saxons established several kingdoms in England.
Many Old English texts originate from the Anglo-Saxons.
